title: Nsight: CUDA-Graph rollback and prefetch residuals (case notes)
content:
Purpose
- Capture Nsight traces and quick triage notes for an intermittent situation where CUDA-graph replay enters a rollback/fallback path and we see residual prefetch activity that correlates with temporary SM occupancy decay and short tail-latency spikes.

Summary of findings (TL;DR)
- Repro rate: ~1-3% of CUDA-graph replays under mixed small/large prompt workload.
- Observable symptom: brief (200–900us) drop in active SM warps and sudden increase in per-kernel latency for subsequent microbatches.
- Root correlation: prefetch/async H2D memcpy overlap with CUDA-graph node sequencing causing the graph executor to serialize certain nodes (internal rollback flag), which triggers a short-lived host-device sync and reduces effective occupancy for ~1–3 kernel launches.
- Impact: 0.5–1.5% P99 latency regression on small-batch tail when this path occurs; not a full outage but noticeable in SLI lab traces.

Testbed and config
- HW: 8x A100-sxm (mixed host). Primary repro node used single A100-SXM instance.
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@commit 2b7f1c3 (CUDA 12.2, cuBLAS/cuDNN matching).
- Model: llama-like 7B v1.2 quantized to q4_0, KV cache enabled, dynamic batching (microbatch size 1–4).
- Batch pattern: randomized small/med/large with 30% short (<64 tokens) requests to maximize microbatch mixing.
- Nsight: nv-nsight-cu-cli 2026.3 (CLI capture with nvtx markers enabled around batch boundaries).
- CUDA-graph usage: graphs recorded per model-shape and replayed across microbatches; we use manual graph capture + replay with a prefetch H2D stage (cudaMemcpyAsync) scheduled into a separate stream.

Capture and profiling notes
- Capture flags used (CLI):
  nv-nsight-cu-cli --target-processes all --profile-from-start off --trace smooth --sample-mode timeline --output nn-cg-rollback-2026-09-15.nvtx
- NVTX markers inserted: BATCH_START/BATCH_END, GRAPH_RECORD_START/GRAPH_RECORD_END, PREFETCH_START/PREFETCH_END, KERNEL_LAUNCH_<name>.
- In traces that hit the issue we observed:
  - A sequence: PREFETCH_END -> GRAPH_REPLAY_START -> small memcpy (async H2D) still inflight -> graph executor raises internal 'resync' and serializes execution -> HOST->DEVICE stream sync invoked (gpu-side small stall) -> graph re-enters replay path but with warmed KV-cache misses -> subsequent small kernels run with 12–18% fewer active warps (occupancy drop) for next 1–3 launches.

Key trace excerpts (translated)
- Timeline snippet (relative time in us):
  0. PREFETCH_START (stream 3)
  120. PREFETCH_END (cudaMemcpyAsync still queued, not complete)
  160. GRAPH_REPLAY_START (stream 0, graph nodes queued)
  180. Device signals rollback flag; executor performs cudaStreamSynchronize(stream3) equivalent
  420. GRAPH_REPLAY_RESUME -> KernelA launch (observed 15% higher latency)
  620. KernelB launch (occupancy still depressed)

Observations from Nsight counters
- SM Active Warps: dropped from baseline 78% -> 63% during affected launches.
- Warp Efficiency: 98% -> 86% (indicating less parallel work rather than inefficiency in execution).
- L2 Hit Rate: unchanged (so not a caching-dominant issue).
- Global Load/Store Throughput: small dip correlated with the occupation drop.
- PCIe/Host Transfer queue: shows short bursts around PREFETCH windows (some retries visible).

Hypotheses considered (and results)
1) Memory alignment in prefetch causing L2/DRAM stalls -> Rejected. L2 metrics steady; stalls happen before kernel memory traffic.
2) Graph node ordering + stream priority inversion -> Plausible. When prefetch async copy uses a lower priority stream, the graph replay attempts to assume it is complete and detects it is not -> causes executor to issue a fallback sync.
3) Driver/CUDA graph bug triggered by certain interleaving patterns -> Possible; repro on CUDA 12.1 and 12.2, but slightly lower repro rate on 12.3 preview. Filed JIRA INF-4829 to track driver-level investigation.

Quick experiments and outcomes
- Move prefetch memcpy to the same stream used for graph node launches (serialize by design): repro rate dropped to <0.1% but overall latency slightly increased due to stricter serialization.
- Use stream priorities (prefetch high-priority): repro rate dropped to ~0.2% and no host-sync observed, occupancy maintained.
- Add cudaEvent + cudaStreamWaitEvent instead of cudaMemcpyAsync naive overlap: reduced repro but added scheduling overhead; net P50 similar, P99 improved.
- Removed CUDA graphs entirely (fall back to kernel launches): issue disappears (expected) but cost of CPU-side overhead increases.

Root cause synthesis
- The serving runtime attempted to maximize concurrency by issuing prefetch async H2D copies in a helper stream while recording/launching CUDA graphs on the primary compute stream. The graph executor's heuristics (and possibly driver behavior) assume captured nodes are self-contained; when an external async H2D is still inflight at replay time, the executor chooses to serialize/rollback to maintain correctness, which results in a short-lived host-device sync and reduces effective SM occupancy for a few launches as the scheduling window slides.

Immediate mitigations implemented (temporary)
- Default change in prefetch scheduling: for small-batch-heavy tenants, prefer stream-priority alignment (set prefetch stream to same priority as compute stream) and emit an explicit cudaEvent & wait before graph replay when prefetch started within 500us of replay. This change is behind flag: runtime.flag.graph_prefetch_strict.
- Add telemetry: count graph-rollbacks and tag traces with graph_prefetch_strict value; surface in Console under per-route perf anomalies.

Longer-term options (tradeoffs)
- Option A: Always schedule prefetches into compute stream (simplicity, predictable correctness) — cost: reduced overlap, slightly higher average latency.
- Option B: Keep overlap but use strict event synchronization (cudaEvent/cudaStreamWaitEvent) and conservative timeouts — cost: extra API calls and potential tiny stalls.
- Option C: Driver-level coordination (work with NVIDIA) to avoid executor fallback for well-known safe patterns — requires driver change and longer lead time.
- Option D: Change capture policy to include prefetch copies inside the graph capture (i.e., record copy nodes as part of graph) — cost: graph explosion for many shape variants and complexity for memory lifetime management.

Action items
- [Aisha] Push runtime.flag.graph_prefetch_strict to canary clusters for two weeks (INF-4829 linked).
- [Jonah] Add automated microbench that fuzzes prefetch timing relative to graph replay to measure repro surface (GH PR #912).
- [Priya] Work with platform to record additional NVTX markers for async copy enqueue vs completion to better distinguish queued vs completed prefetch operations in SLO traces.
- [Mateo] Open an upstream bug report with NVIDIA including attached .nvvp sample and sequence diagram (INF-4829).

Notes for oncall / SRE
- Signal: sudden, small P99 jump for a subset of routes where small-batch mixing is common.
- Tag in alert pipeline: graph-rollbacks (new metric) should trigger investigation but not paging if <0.5% across cluster.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Minimal capture command we used:
  nv-nsight-cu-cli --target-processes all --profile-from-start off --trace compute,api --sample-mode timeline --output out.nvtx \n    --csv-output out.csv --sections sm_activity,l2,mem__pwr

- Example nvprof/nvtx insertion (pseudocode):
  nvtxRangePushA("PREFETCH_START");
  cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, prefetchStream);
  nvtxRangePop();

- Quick check to detect rollback occurrences in logs: search for executor logs with keys: \"graph-resync\", \"rollback\", \"host-sync\"

Closing thoughts
- This is an expensive but low-rate edge-case that mostly affects tail latency for small-batch-heavy traffic.
- The pragmatic path is to ship the stream-priority + event-wait mitigations and continue to partner with NVIDIA to identify if a driver-level race exists.
- We'll monitor the new metric and surface to product owners for tenant-level opt-in if needed (dedicated vs hosted tiers).

Draft history
- 2026-09-15 initial capture and notes (Aisha)
- 2026-09-21 added micro-experiment results (Jonah)
- 2026-09-30 mitigation flag introduced and canary rollout started (Aisha/PR #912)
- 2026-10-02 updated with driver-level followup and action items (Priya)
